subject_area: Mobile application programming — Android with iOS/Swift intro
pedagogical_level: undergraduate fundamentals course with hands-on Android implementation
course_intent: Teach students to build native Android applications using the Android SDK and Java — students should leave able to design Android UIs, manage activity/fragment lifecycles, persist data with SQLite, communicate via intents and broadcast receivers, integrate maps and location services, and handle background work, with a brief introduction to iOS/Swift game development.
depth_bound: Recommendations stay at the level of Android SDK fundamentals and hands-on app construction (Java-based, single-app focus). Modern Kotlin-first idioms, Jetpack Compose, advanced architecture patterns (MVVM, Clean Architecture), reactive frameworks (RxJava, Coroutines, Flow), CI/CD for mobile, and cross-platform frameworks (Flutter, React Native) beyond brief mention are out of scope.
key_topics: Android architecture stack and Dalvik/ART runtime
Activity lifecycle and intents (explicit, implicit, sub-activities with results)
UI building with layouts, widgets, and fragments (static/dynamic)
SQLite persistence via SQLiteOpenHelper, Cursors, and ContentValues
Content Providers and ContentResolver (custom and built-in like Contacts)
Broadcast Receivers (manifest-registered and dynamic) for system/custom intents
Background work with AsyncTask, Threads, and Handlers; ANR avoidance
Google Maps integration, Geocoder, and location-based services with permissions
Introduction to iOS development with Swift basics and Xcode
one_liner: Hands-on undergraduate Android application development course using Java and the Android SDK, covering UI, lifecycle, persistence, intents, background work, and maps — does NOT cover Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, modern architecture patterns, reactive programming, or cross-platform frameworks beyond a brief Swift/iOS intro.
